text.p: Hollinger International Inc officially ended the London broadsheet price war on Thursday, saying that its Daily Telegraph newspaper would hike its cover price starting next week, matching a recent increase by Rupert Murdoch's The Times.

The Telegraph will mirror The Times' five pence a copy price rise from Tuesday to Friday, and will bump up the Saturday price five pence versus a 10 pence rise in the Saturday Times. It will also end a voucher system.
Hollinger said the latest moves would add almost US$20 million to The Telegraph's annualized pre-tax profit.
Like its arch rival, The Telegraph will also cancel a voucher system for the Tuesday paper that allowed participating readers to purchase it for 10 pence.
Hollinger said the increases will pull circulation revenues back nearly to the levels which preceded the price war between the two London-based broadsheet newspapers.

"And, along with substantial year over year advertising revenue increases, (the price increases) will raise The Telegraph's operating profit levels to the highest point in the company's history," Hollinger said.
Beginning in the fourth quarter, current circulation and operating margins at The Daily and Sunday Telegraphs will be well above previous projections, Hollinger said.

"The Daily Telegraph emerges from this period of almost unprecedented intense competition with a steadily rising circulation, and a younger and more prosperous readership than at any time since reliable data was available," said Hollinger chairman and chief executive Conrad Black in a statement.
"These developments should make even higher levels of profitability achievable," he added.
Black said The Telegraph's circulation has risen to its highest point in recent years.
Hollinger Inc owns 57.8 percent of Hollinger International which in turn owns The Telegraph.
